about: Every limit the app's look, feel and speed are held to, each a number with its reason and the tool that measures it (stage B of the audit). A limit is never loosened: where a measure of today exists (`today`), the limit is no looser than it (e2e/__tests__/limits.test.ts), and every limit is fixed for good at the code that enters the zero rounds. `pending-owner` marks the numbers held to the best app of its kind, which wait for the owner's test Google account on the emulator; `pending-lab` marks a measure whose first record comes from the speed lab's feel run (or, for the download, from the Sealed E2E job's build); `launch-time` marks a number only the launch build can give, with its trigger, never written before it. A limit kept in another file is named there (`in`), never copied.

tapResponse.reason: The physical floor: a tap is answered on the very next frame of a 60 Hz screen, 1000/60 ms after the touch. No app answers sooner; every frame later is a delay a member can feel.

layoutJumps.reason: The physical floor: nothing a member reads moves while no one touches the screen. One move is a jump.

jsFrameP95.reason: The app's own JavaScript work in a frame while scrolling, at the 95th percentile: half of a 60 Hz frame, leaving the other half to the UI thread's mount and the draw. Absolute, because it is the runner's real CPU, not its software GPU.

jsFrameWorst.reason: No frame of a scroll holds the JS thread for more than the whole frame (1000/60 ms): one that does drops the frame whatever the GPU.

commitScrolling.reason: A React commit while the list scrolls fits one frame (1000/60 ms): a longer one holds the JS thread past the frame the scroll needed it for.

commitLongest.reason: Any one React commit, opening a page included: RAIL (web.dev) calls a task over 50 ms long, since it delays the answer to the next touch past 100 ms.

tripsInARow.reason: A page at its floor waits on one round trip at most, none when it holds what it draws. Today the member page's deepest opening waits on 2 (Sealed E2E logs of 2026-11-08): over its floor.

afterAnswer.reason: A page at its floor draws within one frame of its last answer (1000/60 ms); the time past it is the speed record's gap, which stage D closes screen by screen.

screenReady.reason: Each screen's opening, median and once, derived from its own recorded history by ceilingsFrom (e2e/screen-times.mjs): a ceiling only falls as the history does.

frameBudget.reason: Drawing time judged against a plain control page measured in the same run, because the lab's graphics are slow software (FRAME-BUDGET-DESIGN).

bundleBytes.reason: The JavaScript the phones get, a ratchet that grows only by a reason in a commit.

downloadBytes.reason: What a member downloads, part by part: no byte without a reason, each growth in the ledger with its commit. Its first record is CI's measure of the Android release build in the Sealed E2E job (x86_64).

downloadBytesStore.trigger: the launch build: the store's own AAB, its download per device as Play reports it
downloadBytesStore.reason: The store build is not the one CI builds, so its download is measured on the launch build itself, by the same parts, and never written before it exists.

coldStart.reason: Held to the best app of its kind, measured on the same emulator signed into the owner's test Google account; where that cannot be measured, to the framework floor below.

memory.reason: Held to the best app of its kind on the same emulator; where that cannot be measured, to the framework floor below.

imageWeight.reason: What opening a screen downloads, held to the best app of its kind on the same emulator.

frameworkFloor.reason: An empty app built exactly as ours is (Expo SDK 57, the same config, e2e/lab/floor-app.mjs), its cold start and memory measured on the same emulator: what no tuning of ours can beat. A best app under it goes to the owner as a dated decision.
